title: Prompt Caching and Cost Control
brief: Your support agent carries a 20,000-token prefix on every call: the full policy manual plus tool schemas. It never changes between calls, yet you pay full price for it on every turn of every ticket. Each ticket takes 3 or 4 turns. Get the average cost under $0.18 per ticket while keeping at least 90% of answers correct.

tasks.label: Partial refund
tasks.prompt: I was charged for 3 seats but only use 2. Can I get the difference back? (dana@example.com)

tasks.label: EU return
tasks.prompt: Order B-7712 arrived in Berlin and I want to return it. How long do I have?

tasks.label: Upgrade proration
tasks.prompt: If I upgrade to the Team plan today, what do I pay this month? Order C-0031.

check_manual.text: Checks section 4.2 of the policy manual (already in the system prompt): EU customers get 30 days, everyone else 14. Proration is daily.

done.text: You are in the EU, so you have 30 days from delivery (until 2 November). I've emailed a prepaid return label.

wrong.text: You have 14 days to return it. (Wrong: the manual gives EU customers 30 days.)

modifiers.note: The small model misreads the long manual more often.

hints: Open the Trace tab. How many input tokens does each turn bill, and how much of that is the same 20,000-token prefix?
A smaller model is cheaper but gets the policy wrong. The manual is identical on every call, so it does not need to be billed in full every time.
Select the model and switch on "Cache stable prefix". The prefix comes first and never changes, so from turn 2 it bills at 10%.
explain: Caching pays off because the expensive part of the prompt is stable and sits at the front. Every turn after the first reads it from cache at a tenth of the price, and the answers do not change.
